narrative.overview: SVGOLOT feels like an inspection bench for production SVG assets, not a gallery or a marketing shell. The interface stays dark, restrained, and operational so previews, metadata, and markup can sit in one workspace without competing for attention. It rejects decorative dashboard tropes and keeps color reserved for action, selection, and state.
keyCharacteristics: Dark, low-glare shell with blue-green tinted neutrals.
One operational teal accent used for action, selection, and active state.
Native sans typography with a compact fixed scale.
Flat resting surfaces, with elevation reserved for hover, popover, and selected state.
Dense workflow where preview, metadata, settings, and markup remain tightly coupled.

rules.name: The Quiet Shell Rule
rules.body: Neutrals do most of the work. Accent belongs to actions and current state, not decoration.

rules.name: The Inspection Contrast Rule
rules.body: Preview, metadata, and code surfaces must separate clearly without jumping to pure black or pure white.

rules.name: The One-Action Accent Rule
rules.body: Action Teal is the only high-attention accent. Warning, success, and danger colors are for status only.

rules.name: The One-Family Rule
rules.body: Use the native sans stack for headings, buttons, labels, and body text. Do not introduce display typography into operational UI.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: Product UI here uses a fixed scale, not fluid type. Headings stay predictable as layout compresses.

rules.name: The Mono-Where-It-Earns-It Rule
rules.body: Monospace is for markup and machine-facing content only, not decorative labeling.

rules.name: The Resting Flat Rule
rules.body: Shell surfaces, summaries, and panels stay flat while idle. Shadow is a state signal, not a permanent texture.

rules.name: The Floating-Only Rule
rules.body: Popovers and selected cards may lift. Static layout containers separate with borders and tone, not shadow.

dos: Do keep the outer app on Base Ink and reserve brighter neutrals for nested working surfaces.
Do use Action Teal for primary action, current selection, active chips, and focus only.
Do keep important batch state visible in the shell, such as asset count, optimization progress, preview mode, and markup visibility.
Do keep first-run empty states procedural, teaching the workflow rather than advertising the app.
Do use the same rounded and border vocabulary across buttons, chips, cards, settings rows, and inputs.
Do keep code and preview surfaces side by side when space allows, then stack them structurally on narrow screens.
donts: Don't make this feel like a marketing landing page, a playful icon toy, or a generic CRUD admin.
Don't introduce decorative dashboards, loud gradients, novelty motion, or cluttered icon galleries.
Don't turn the asset grid into a gallery with hidden file state. Original size, optimized size, and delta remain visible.
Don't use a second accent color or apply teal broadly to inactive surfaces.
Don't hide optimization state behind vague copy, icon-only cues, or hard-to-scan panel hierarchy.
Don't add nested cards, colored side-stripe callouts, glassmorphism, or glowing hero metrics.
